## Symptom

A `@vitest-environment jsdom` component test that reads a CSS value back out of an
element's serialized inline `style` attribute (`el.getAttribute('style')` /
`el.style.background`) passes locally but fails **intermittently in the fleet's
green-checkpoint / test:affected runs** — reported by the red-test watchdog as
"failed N× in the last 6h" while it is stubbornly green on your box.

Concrete instance (EI-10457): `ClaimAttemptTimeline.test.tsx` asserted

```ts
expect(r2.getAttribute('style') ?? '').toContain('color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent), transparent 92%)');
```

The failure tail showed the row's style as `border-bottom: 1px solid #2e2e2e; cur…`
— the `background` value was **gone**, not wrong.

## Root cause

jsdom's CSSOM is backed by the `cssstyle` package, which **validates every value and
silently drops the ones it can't parse**. Modern CSS functions — `color-mix()`,
`oklch()`/`oklab()`, some `var()` shorthands — are supported only in newer `cssstyle`
versions. On a machine whose resolved `cssstyle`/`jsdom` predates that support, setting
`el.style.background = 'color-mix(…)'` stores nothing, so the value never appears in the
serialized `style` attribute. Support therefore varies **by installed version across the
multi-machine fleet** → the assertion is green where cssstyle is new, red where it's old.
This is version-skew flakiness, not run-to-run flake (it's deterministic per machine).

Confirm which way your box resolves:

```bash
node -e "const {CSSStyleDeclaration}=require('cssstyle'); const s=new CSSStyleDeclaration(); s.background='color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent), transparent 92%)'; console.log(JSON.stringify(s.background))"
# new cssstyle → prints the value; old → prints "" (dropped)
```

## Fix — assert the DECISION, not the round-tripped CSS

jsdom does no layout or paint, so it can never verify what a style actually *renders*.
Testing the exact CSS string is the wrong altitude anyway. Expose the styling **decision**
as a stable `data-*` attribute driven by the same predicate as the visual style, and assert
on that:

```tsx
// component
const isHighlighted = (row) => props.highlightOutcome !== undefined && row.outcome === props.highlightOutcome;
// getRowBg and the data flag share ONE predicate, so the flag can't drift from the paint
getRowBg={(row) => isHighlighted(row) ? 'color-mix(in oklab, var(--accent), transparent 92%)' : undefined}
rowProps={({ row }) => ({ 'data-highlighted': isHighlighted(row) ? 'true' : 'false', /* … */ })}
```

```ts
// test — env-independent
expect(r2.getAttribute('data-highlighted')).toBe('true');
expect(r1.getAttribute('data-highlighted')).toBe('false');
```

## Rule of thumb

In a jsdom unit test, **never assert on a CSS-function value read back from a serialized
`style`/`className`-derived computed style**. Assert a `data-*` (or `aria-*`) attribute that
encodes the same decision the styling is derived from. Save real visual/painted-style
verification for Playwright (`apps/operator/e2e/*.spec.ts`) or the Tauri agent-e2e path,
which run in a real engine.
